verified: 55/55 official names, descriptions and grades verified vs Exophase (2026-11-18) + PSNProfiles; 28 hidden verified vs planetgta6.com + outputlag.com

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: There is no separate task behind this one: it pops the moment the other 54 are earned, so treat it as the end of the roadmap rather than a trophy to chase on its own. Work the seven stages in order — story first, then contacts and strangers, then activities, collectibles and the money grinds — and let A Long Road, 100% completion, be the last gate before it. If any single trophy stalls, open its guide here: each of the 54 carries its own method, its PSN target where PlayStation tracks one, and its sources. Nothing about this trophy can be missed on its own, because it only follows the rest.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (trophy list) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Play the opening mission, Gone Fishing, to its end and this pops with the credits of the intro. It is pure story progress: follow the on-screen objectives, and there is no side requirement, no collectible and no alternate route to worry about. Because it is the first mission, it cannot be missed — every playthrough starts here. It also opens the story chain, so the chapter trophies that follow (Paradise Lost onwards) build directly on it. If you are replaying, it pops again on a fresh save as soon as the mission ends.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (trophy list) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 1 and the trophy pops at the chapter's close. Chapters are unmissable story progress: there is no way to finish the story without clearing them, and no chapter trophy can be skipped by doing side content first. Play the missions in the order the game presents them; the chapter ends on its own once the last mission's objectives are done. Do not worry about medals, collectibles or side activities while clearing a chapter — none of them gate the chapter trophy, and they are all covered by their own trophies later in this guide.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (trophy list) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 2 and the trophy pops at the chapter's close. Like every chapter trophy, it is unmissable: the story cannot advance past Chapter 2 without it, so any playthrough earns it. Work through the missions in the order given; side activities, strangers and collectibles can wait, because none of them is required to close a chapter. If you are tracking the roadmap, Chapter 2 is where the open world starts to widen, so it is a good moment to start the activities sampler in stage 3 between missions rather than leaving every side trophy to the end.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (trophy list) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 3 and the trophy pops at the chapter's close. Chapter trophies are story progress and cannot be missed, so this one is a matter of playing through, not hunting. By Chapter 3 the map and the contact missions are well open: use the gaps between story missions to tick off the contact finals and the stranger strands in stage 2, because those missions unlock as the story advances and finishing them early keeps the endgame grind short. The chapter itself needs nothing but its own missions.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (trophy list) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 4 and the trophy pops at the chapter's close. This is the last chapter trophy before the finale, and like the others it is unmissable story progress. By now most of the map, contacts and activities are open, so before the final mission it pays to clear the contact finals (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) and the eight stranger strands — those are the stage 2 trophies, and they are easier to finish while the story still sends you across Leonida than after the credits, when you would be travelling only for them.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (trophy list) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: Play the final mission to its end. This is the story's closing mission, so it unlocks only after Chapter 4, and it pops as soon as the mission's objectives are complete. Whether the finale branches into a choice is not yet confirmed publicly, so do not assume a second ending is needed: the trophy asks only for the final mission itself, and one completion earns it. Keep a save from before the finale if you want to revisit the ending, but the trophy does not require it. This is the gold that closes stage 1 of the roadmap.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (trophy list) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Breakfast Run. Mission trophies are single-mission clears: take the mission when the game offers it, follow its objectives, and the trophy pops at the mission's end. There is no extra condition — no medal, no time limit and no collectible inside the mission is required. If the mission ever fails, replaying it is free and the trophy pops on the successful run. Breakfast Run sits early in the story, so most players earn it on their first pass through the campaign without going out of their way.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (trophy list) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission The Cartel Heist. As with every named-mission trophy, the requirement is the mission itself: start it when it appears, finish its objectives, and the trophy pops at the end. No medal or optional objective is needed, and a failed attempt costs nothing — replay the mission and it pops on the clear. Heist missions tend to be longer than ordinary ones, so expect several phases inside the single mission, but the trophy still only asks for the one completion.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (trophy list) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Child's Play. The trophy is the mission clear itself: accept it when it appears in the story, play it through, and it pops when the mission ends. There is no hidden requirement — no collectible to grab inside it and no medal to earn. If you fail the mission, restart it from the checkpoint or the mission select; the trophy pops on the first successful completion. Like the other mission trophies, it is unmissable as long as you play the story to the end.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (trophy list) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners. One mission, one trophy: start it when the story offers it, finish its objectives, and it pops at the mission's end. No medal, no optional objective and no collectible inside the mission is required, and a failed run can simply be replayed. Mission trophies like this one are the backbone of stage 1 — they fall naturally as you play the campaign, so there is nothing to plan around them beyond finishing the story.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (trophy list) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission VCIA Takedown. The trophy is the mission clear: take it when it appears, complete its objectives, and it pops when the mission ends. The name points at the airport — VCIA is Vice City International Airport — and the mission plays out there, but the trophy itself asks for nothing beyond the clear, so no special preparation is needed. If the mission fails, replay it; the trophy pops on the first successful run. It pairs naturally with Catch Me If You Can, the other VCIA trophy, though that one is a separate open-world moment rather than this mission.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (trophy list) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Operation Savage Glory. As with the other named missions, the trophy is the clear itself: start the mission, finish its objectives, and it pops at the end. No medal or side objective gates it, and a failed attempt can be replayed freely. This is the last of the named-mission trophies in stage 1; once it pops, the story trophies left are the chapter closes and the final mission, so the campaign is nearly done and the side stages of the roadmap take over.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (trophy list) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Reach 100% on the game's completion counter. This is the long gate before the platinum: it counts the story, the stranger strands, the collectibles and the activities together, so it only pops once every other counted thing is done. Use the in-game stats or progress screen as the checklist — it shows which categories are still short — and work the lowest ones first. The exact 100% checklist is not yet fully mapped in public guides, so expect a few categories to surprise you near the end; this guide's roadmap stages 1 to 6 cover every counted trophy, and clearing them all is the practical route to 100%. Treat this as the final trophy, not an early one.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN count: 100%) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunts. A stunt is a driving feat the game counts — jumps, airtime, near misses and the like — and PlayStation tracks the total to 250, so this is a volume trophy, not a skill gate: every stunt you pull anywhere in Leonida counts toward it. The fastest route is to fold stunts into normal driving rather than grinding them in one place: take jumps and fast runs whenever you travel, and the counter climbs on its own. Use the counter in the guide pane to track progress, and expect this to pop during the collectible and exploration stages, when you are driving the most. It cannot be missed, because stunts are available from the start and the counter never resets.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN count: 250) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each of the nine activity types once. The trophy only asks for one attempt at each type — not a win, not a medal, just trying it — so it is one of the cheapest trophies in the game. Open the activities list in the game and work down it: one race, one fishing spot, one arcade game, one shooting-range challenge and so on until all nine types show as tried. PlayStation tracks the count to nine. Do this early, in stage 3, because trying everything once also shows you which activities you enjoy enough to grind for their own trophies (races, fishing, the range) and which you can leave alone.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN count: 9) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges. This is the skill trophy of the set: 42 separate range challenges, each needing a gold-medal score. Learn one weapon and one range at a time rather than rushing all 42 — the challenges share mechanics, so the accuracy and speed habits from the first few carry over. Replay any challenge freely; only the best medal counts, and a gold on a challenge stays earned. Expect this to take the longest of the activity trophies, so start it in stage 4 and chip away between other stages. No challenge is missable: the ranges stay open after the story.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN count: 42) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at all 14 locations. Each location has its own drone race, and the trophy needs a win at every one of them — not just 14 wins anywhere. Work through the locations one by one; a win at a location stays won, so you can clear them in any order and across sessions. Drone races reward clean lines over raw speed, so learn each course's corners before pushing for the win, and replay a location freely if you lose — there is no penalty for retrying. The 14 locations are spread across Leonida, so this also doubles as a tour of the map for the exploration trophy.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN count: 14) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races. The key word is different: winning the same race 20 times does not count — PlayStation tracks 20 distinct race wins. Enter a spread of races across the map (street, off-road and whatever other types the game lists) and win each one once. Losing is free, so replay any race until you win it, then move on to the next new one. This pairs well with the drone races and the activity sampler: while you are trying every activity once for Master of None, note which races suit you, then return for the 20 wins. Races stay available after the story, so nothing here can be missed.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN count: 20) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Cal is the fishing rival: find his challenge at a fishing spot, enter it, and out-fish him. A fishing challenge is a head-to-head catch contest, so the method is the fishing itself — cast, hook and reel in cleanly — rather than any gear trick. If you lose, challenge him again; there is no limit on attempts and no penalty for losing. One win is all the trophy asks. Fishing spots are also where the opening mission's fishing happens, so the mechanic is one you already know from the story; the challenge is simply doing it better than Cal once.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (trophy list) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game. Find an arcade machine in the world, start any game on it, and play it to its end — a full completion, not just starting it. Any arcade game counts, so pick the shortest or easiest one you find and finish it. There is no score requirement and no second game needed. Arcade machines are scattered through Leonida's indoor spots, and this is the quickest of the activity-sampler trophies: one game, one trophy, and it also counts as one of the nine activity types for Master of None.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (trophy list) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Andy. Contact missions form a chain: each contact gives a series of missions, and this trophy pops when Andy's last one is done. Take Andy's missions whenever they appear — they unlock as the story advances — and keep going until no more appear for him. The trophy is the final mission's clear, with no extra condition. Contact chains are unmissable in the sense that the missions stay available once unlocked, but they can be left undone for a long time, so clear them as they appear rather than saving all five contacts for the endgame.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (trophy list) · planetgta6.com + outputlag.com (hidden status) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Kenton. Like Andy's chain, Kenton's missions arrive as a series across the story, and this trophy pops on the last one. Play Kenton's missions when they appear and follow the chain to its end; the final mission's clear is the whole requirement. There is no medal or optional objective attached. Because contact missions unlock with story progress, a chain can sit unfinished for chapters if you ignore it — check your contacts between story missions and clear whatever is waiting, so stage 2 finishes alongside the campaign instead of becoming a post-story chore.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (trophy list) · planetgta6.com + outputlag.com (hidden status) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Billy. Billy's missions come as a chain like the other contacts': take them as they unlock, play them in order, and this trophy pops when the last one is complete. The requirement is the final mission's clear alone — no medal, no side objective. Contact chains are easy to postpone and easy to forget, so the practical advice is the same for all five contacts: never let a contact sit with a waiting mission for more than a chapter. Finish Billy's chain and one more stage 2 trophy is done.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (trophy list) · planetgta6.com + outputlag.com (hidden status) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across Leonida. Strangers are the odd characters marked around the state, each with a short strand of missions; the trophy needs eight complete strands, and PlayStation tracks the count to eight. Explore the map and take every stranger marker you pass — strands unlock as you travel, and each one is only a few missions long. A strand counts when its last mission is done, so always finish a strand you start rather than leaving it half done. Eight strands is the requirement, not all of them: if one strand stalls, another stranger elsewhere will cover the count.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN count: 8) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Randy. Randy's chain works like the other contacts': a series of missions that unlocks with story progress, ending in a final mission whose clear pops the trophy. Play Randy's missions as they appear and do not let the chain idle — the five contact finals are stage 2, and they are meant to be finished while the story still carries you around Leonida. No medal or optional objective is required; the final mission's completion is the whole trophy.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (trophy list) · planetgta6.com + outputlag.com (hidden status) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Tyrone. Tyrone is the fifth contact chain: take his missions as they unlock, follow them to the last one, and the trophy pops on its completion. Like the other contact finals it asks only for the final mission's clear, with no medal or side condition. With Tyrone done, all five contact chains are finished and stage 2 is nearly complete — only the stranger strands and Bret's hunt remain. If a contact's missions ever seem to stop appearing, advance the story a mission or two: chains unlock with story progress, not with time.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (trophy list) · planetgta6.com + outputlag.com (hidden status) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 spots across Leonida. This is the one trophy on a missable watch: meditation spots are tied to places you visit as the story moves, and no public guide has yet confirmed whether every spot stays reachable after the story ends — so do not leave them. The rule is simple: whenever you find a meditation spot, meditate there on the spot instead of telling yourself you will come back. PlayStation tracks the count to 18. Spots are spread across the state, so this also rewards the exploration in stage 5. If a spot will not trigger, check that you are standing in the marked place and that no mission is currently locking the area.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN count: 18) · planetgta6.com (no confirmed missable list yet — 'We can't tell yet') · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret. Bret's strand is a hunt: take his mission, track the unique animal he names, and take it down. A unique animal is a one-off quarry rather than ordinary wildlife, so follow the mission's tracking prompts instead of wandering — the hunt leads you to it. The trophy pops when the hunt's objective completes. It sits in stage 2 with the stranger strands because it is a stranger's mission chain, and like the other stranger missions it stays available once unlocked. Bring a scoped weapon and patience; the animal will not be standing in the open.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (trophy list) · planetgta6.com + outputlag.com (hidden status) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete 3 collectible card sets. Cards are hidden around Leonida in sets, and the trophy needs three full sets — not three cards. Pick up every card you pass while exploring, and use the in-game collection screen to see which sets are close to complete so you can hunt the missing cards deliberately instead of wandering. Cards are not missable: they stay where they are after the story, so this is a patient stage 5 trophy. PlayStation tracks the count to three sets. A set only counts when its last card is collected, so a set with one card missing is worth nothing until you find it.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN count: 3) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Use WAiNK It at 100 locations. WAiNK It is the game's photo or check-in action at marked locations — visit a location, use it there, and the location counts. PlayStation tracks the total to 100, so this is a volume collectible: every new place you visit is a chance to add one. The practical route is to fold it into exploration for The Goodtime State (52 areas) and the card hunt: whenever you reach a new spot, WAiNK It before leaving. Locations stay available after the story, so nothing here can be missed, but 100 is a lot — start early in stage 5 and keep the habit all the way through the endgame.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN count: 100) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges. Challenges are the game's side objectives — small tasks scattered across activities, combat, driving and exploration — and PlayStation tracks the count to 50. This is a volume trophy that fills itself in: by the time you have done the races, the range, the stunts and the collectibles, a large share of the 50 is already done. Check the challenges list in the game for what is left and pick the easy ones first; a challenge counts the moment it completes, and completed challenges never un-complete. It cannot be missed, because challenges are available throughout and after the story.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN count: 50) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Lose a 4-star wanted level while your partner is with you, and escape. Build the wanted level to four stars with your partner present — committing crimes in front of the police is the reliable way — then break line of sight and stay hidden until the stars clear. The trophy pops when the wanted level drops to zero with your partner still with you. The trick is the escape, not the crime: use alleys, tunnels or fast driving to break the search, and do not start a new crime while hiding or the level climbs again. Your partner must be with you for the whole escape, so do not let them get left behind or arrested.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (trophy list) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner, without losing your wanted level. The run is the puzzle: rob one shop, move straight to the next, rob it, then a third — all with your partner, and all while keeping a wanted level active the whole time. If the wanted level clears between shops, the chain breaks and you start over. Plan a route of three close shops before you start, keep the robberies quick, and avoid anything that would clear the heat (like hiding long enough to lose the stars) until the third shop is done. The trophy pops on the third robbery. A failed chain costs nothing but the attempt.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN count: 3) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles. A vehicle counts as discovered the first time you enter or drive it, and PlayStation tracks the total to 100 — so variety matters, not mileage. Leonida is full of distinct cars, bikes, boats and more; every new model you get into adds one. The fastest route is to try everything you pass: hop into a new vehicle whenever you see one instead of always taking the same car. This pairs with On the Spot (register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app) and with exploration — new areas have new vehicles. Nothing here can be missed: vehicles stay available after the story.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN count: 100) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus. Combat Focus is the slow-aim mode: trigger it when several enemies are in front of you, and drop five of them before it ends. The setup matters more than the aim — wait for a moment when enemies are grouped, then activate it and work through them quickly, because the mode lasts only a short time. A crowded fight or a mission with clustered enemies is the place to try it; a quiet street with one enemy at a time is not. If you only get three or four, the count resets, so try again in the next grouped fight. No special weapon is required.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN count: 5) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA — Vice City International Airport. The trophy is an open-world moment, not a mission: get to the airport, get hold of a plane, and take off without a scheduled flight. Any aircraft on the tarmac will do; the point is the departure itself, leaving the airport by air on your own terms. The airport is the same place as the VCIA Takedown mission, so you will know the layout from the story — but this trophy is separate from that mission and can be done any time you can reach a plane. Expect a wanted level on the way out; that is part of the fun, not a failure.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (trophy list) · planetgta6.com + outputlag.com (hidden status) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: Deal with Rhinos — the tanks. The description is a joke about the heat inside a Rhino, and the trophy is about the tank itself: get into one, or take one on, in the open world. Rhinos appear when the wanted level is high, so the reliable route is to raise the heat until the military responds, then either steal a Rhino or destroy it — the trophy is about the encounter, and either outcome in the moment counts as dealing with it. Exactly which interaction pops it is not yet pinned down in public guides, so try the steal first: climbing into a Rhino is the more distinctive act, and it is also the more useful one afterwards.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (trophy list) · planetgta6.com + outputlag.com (hidden status) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected. This is a stealth robbery: get in, take the goods and get out before any alarm or witness raises the alert. Plan the approach — enter quietly, avoid the cameras and the staff's line of sight, take what you came for and leave before anyone notices. If you are spotted, the attempt fails, so leave and try again; a failed attempt costs nothing but the trip. Pick a quiet hour in the game world if the store is busy, and do not bring a weapon out — the trophy is about not being detected, and a drawn gun is the fastest way to be noticed.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (trophy list) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape. Each vault is a robbery plus a getaway: crack the vault, take the money, and get clear of the police before the trophy counts it. PlayStation tracks the count to five, and a vault only counts when the escape succeeds — dying or getting caught after the robbery does not count it. Plan the getaway before the robbery, not after: know your exit route and your vehicle, and break line of sight fast once you are out. Vaults are spread across Leonida, so this also moves you around the map; do them one at a time between other stages rather than all five in a row.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN count: 5) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Armored trucks travel the roads of Leonida: stop one, force it open, take the cash and get clear before the police close in. The robbery is the easy half — the escape is what the trophy counts, so have a fast vehicle ready and a route away from the main roads before you start. A failed escape means the attempt does not count, so do not linger at the truck once the money is yours. One successful robbery and escape is all it asks; trucks keep appearing, so a failed run is just a reason to try the next one.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (trophy list) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore all 52 areas of Leonida. An area counts when you have visited it, and PlayStation tracks the total to 52 — so this is the map-completion trophy. The practical route is to drive the whole state deliberately: use the in-game map to spot the areas you have never entered, then visit them one by one rather than hoping to stumble into all 52. This pairs with everything in stage 5 — WAiNK It locations, cards, vehicles and meditation spots are all found by exploring — so do it while hunting those, and the areas fill in together. Nothing here can be missed: every area stays reachable after the story.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN count: 52) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each of the nine gangs. Every gang runs illegal operations somewhere in Leonida, and the trophy needs one robbery from each gang — nine in total, one per gang, not nine from the same gang. Find an operation, rob it, and move on to the next gang's. The operations are marked in the world once you know what to look for, so the hunt is the work: learn which operations belong to which gang and tick them off one by one. A robbery that fails does not count, but operations can be retried. This is a stage 4 trophy that rewards knowing the map's gangs rather than brute force.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN count: 9) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. This is a quiet moment trophy: go to Ocean Beach, find the spot with the view — a bar or a beachfront seat — and order the cocktail. There is no challenge and no timer; the trophy pops when the moment happens. Ocean Beach is the Vice City shoreline, so head for the beachfront and look for the place to sit and drink. It is the kind of trophy that is easy to walk past while chasing bigger things, so make the trip deliberately in stage 5, when you are exploring the coast for areas and WAiNK It spots anyway.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style. Drive into a vehicle showroom, then drive straight back out through the glass — the classic GTA exit. Any showroom will do; the trophy is the act itself, and it pops as soon as you are out through the front. Expect a wanted level and a repair bill, and expect it to be worth it: pick a fast car, line up the exit before you enter, and floor it through the glass in one run. If the first attempt only cracks the glass, reverse and try again — the trophy wants the full smash-out, not a scratch.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Follow through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley. Go to the bowling alley, start a game, and bowl — the trophy is about the follow-through, the act of playing a frame through rather than just showing up. Any game counts, and there is no score requirement, so play a frame or two and it pops. The alley is a named place in the world, so head for Kolt & Associates when you are in the area. It pairs with Ten Pin, the melee drive-by trophy, only by name — the two are separate moments, and this one is the calm one.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: Make choices — 500 of them, by PlayStation's count. The trophy tracks the choices you make across the game: dialogue choices, approach choices, the small decisions the game keeps offering. It is a volume trophy, not a single decision: keep choosing, in missions and in the open world, and the counter climbs toward 500. There is no right or wrong choice for this trophy — the description says 'for better or worse', and the count is what matters. It will likely pop late, during the long grinds of stage 6, so do not grind it deliberately early; just keep making choices whenever the game offers them, and let the counter do the work.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: This is one of the three trophies whose trigger is not yet confirmed in public guides, so this guide will not invent one. trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: This is one of the three trophies whose trigger is not yet confirmed in public guides, so this guide will not invent one. trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Bowl someone over with a melee drive-by. A melee drive-by is hitting a person with a melee weapon from a moving vehicle — drive past your target and swing as you pass, knocking them down like a bowling pin. Pick a slow vehicle and a clear stretch so you can line the pass up, and aim for a lone pedestrian rather than a crowd. One knockdown is all the trophy asks. It is the rowdy sibling of Let's Go Bowling, and like that trophy it is a single moment: once you have the timing, it pops on the first clean hit. If you miss, circle back and try the pass again.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 by laundering marked bills through your contacts. Marked bills are the dirty money from robberies and heists; contacts clean it for a cut. The route is to keep earning marked bills — vaults, trucks, shops — and keep laundering them through contacts until the clean total reaches $250,000. PlayStation tracks the count to 250,000, and it is a long grind by design, so fold it into the rest of the game: every robbery in stage 4 feeds this total. Do not spend the laundered money before the trophy pops if you can help it — the count is what you have earned by laundering, and the grind is shorter when the money keeps flowing one way.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN count: $250,000) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops. Every dollar you spend in any shop counts — clothes, weapons, food, car parts — and PlayStation tracks the total to $100,000. This is the spending twin of the laundering trophy: the money you clean in Dime on the Dollar is the money you spend here. Buy the gear you actually want first (weapons and vehicles are the big tickets), then top the total up with whatever is left when you are close. It cannot be missed, because shops stay open after the story, and it will likely pop on its own during a normal playthrough that buys gear along the way.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN count: $100,000) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Purchase all 8 garage properties. Garages are the properties that store your vehicles, and the trophy needs all eight bought. They go on sale as you progress and earn money, so check the property listings whenever you have cash to spare and buy each garage as it appears. Eight is the total PlayStation tracks, and a garage only counts once it is yours. Garages are also practical — they are where the 100 discovered vehicles from Whip It Good end up living — so buy them as you go rather than saving all eight for the endgame, when the money is already spent elsewhere.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN count: 8) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. The Scooter Bros app is the in-game service for registering vehicles: take a vehicle you have discovered, open the app, and register it. Ten registrations is the count PlayStation tracks. This pairs directly with Whip It Good (discover 100 vehicles) — every new vehicle you find is a registration candidate, so register the first ten you discover and the trophy pops early in stage 5. Registrations stay valid, and the app stays available after the story, so nothing here can be missed. If a vehicle will not register, check that it is one you discovered yourself rather than a mission-only vehicle.
trophies.sources: Exophase (official list: name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN count: 10) · Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.
